story:
It started as a petty contest of pride.――No, calling it a start might be misleading; even now, as the end is finally in sight, it’s nothing more than that same petty contest of pride.

What a truly fruitless squabble. So, I’d declared my dropout early on and shifted to a neutral position, one that had nothing to do with winning or losing.

Or so I thought――,

“Mistress―! Whaddya think, whaddya think, I reckon it turned out pretty darn great from my angle, but I want ya to give it a fair and square judgment, no favoritism, straight-up from your eyes!”

“Hah? Don’t mess with me, you punk—does that kinda nonsense fly anywhere? Hey, you— if you go along with this idiot’s crap, you’re in for it. You’re pourin’ drinks till dawn tonight, so get that through your thick skull, got it?”

“Threatenin’ her like that ain’t playin’ fair, is it? And hey, not that long ago, you were trash-talkin’ that girl left and right, callin’ her a brat or a shrimp or whatever. Now you flip-flop and pull this? That’s straight-up sly, don’tcha think—what’s your take?”

“Shut your trap, don’t gimme that weird half-baked way of talkin’, you. Like I’d let words from some jackass I can’t even understand land on me, you idiot.”

Amid the rowdy hubbub of voices, I let out a small sigh and gazed out at the white sandy beach.

There, two castles stood. Made of sand, their construction crude. But their size—that alone rivaled the real thing with its sheer imposing scale.

The so-called sandcastles――,

“Which one, Mistress! Which one’s closer to the real-deal castle! Gimme your honest opinion as a doting mom, no holds barred!”

And just like that, saddled with the role of judge in this fruitless feud, I found myself at a total loss.

The two castles before me were modeled after the beautiful one built on an island in the lake beyond the white sand beach where they’d been made—that one was the genuine article. The whole thing had kicked off when one of our group, who had business at that castle, gazed at it from the lakeside shore and offhandedly mentioned, “Back home, we had this game where we’d build castles out of sand.”

“No way! That’s super romantic, right?! Then tonight, we’ll do the charade dance on the balcony of the castle I built, me and Master!”

Shaula’s eyes had sparkled as she latched onto his words, and she dove right into castle-building on the beach.

In the end, with Shaula barred from the castle due to matters of etiquette, and the rest of us unable to enter because of our shady pasts, we were stuck waiting for their return—and what was supposed to be cheering on her sandcastle efforts turned into...

“Before we knew it, it snowballed into a contest over who could build the prettiest castle... Well, it was just Shaula and Reid gettin’ all competitive, but it’s all so innocently childish, y’know.”

“And what, actin’ all detached like some observer playin’ the adult? Mistress, you just plain ran outta steam diggin’ in the sand and tapped out. A parent losin’ to sand? That’s straight-up embarrassin’ for me.”

“Embarrassing’s a bit harsh, isn’t it—embarrassing! First off, I didn’t lose to the sand or anything. I just got fed up with the pointless bickering and wisely bowed out, that’s all.”

“Yeeah, sure thing, Mistress—you’re so great, so great. Want me to give ya a lift-up?”

“Maybe show a little more respect for your parent! Instead of ‘great-great’ or ‘up you go,’ how about ‘amazing-amazing’ or something!”

“If that’s what works for ya, fine by me, but I can’t really tell the difference.”

Alec let out a wry chuckle at that, and I puffed out my cheeks with a “mmph,” falling silent.

What bubbled up inside me was a mix of feeling bested and genuine admiration for his way with words. For it to actually sound coherent was a huge step forward.

“Anything worth doing takes the most energy right at the start, when you’re building something new. To forge unity from words like this—it’s a clever idea. Even I’m impressed.”

“Aw, c’mon, most of it’s just me leanin’ on other folks’ smarts, y’know. But once it clicks, I reckon it’ll turn into somethin’ pretty solid.”

“Yeah, I think so too. I’m the same way――hyaaah!?”

Mid-conversation, a finger trailed down my back, and I jolted upright on reflex. Looking over, there was that infuriating redhead right behind me, cackling like an idiot: “Ka-kka-kka-kka!”

“Why you—put a little more oomph in that scream, huh? You yelped like you spotted a bug—total mood-killer, you know that?”

“W-What kinda talk is that? Touchin’ people so casually... And like Alec said, you never had any interest in me before!”

“That was back when you were still a squirt, duh. Now your height, arms, legs—they’ve all stretched out, and your boobs and butt got bigger... Not quite enough to satisfy, but hey, they did. So that makes you a woman, woman.”

“Pass. No thanks. The thought of you treatin’ me like a woman gives me the chills. And I’m not pourin’ drinks either. If you wanna booze, go do it with the folks who actually wanna drink—till dawn, whatever.”

“What’s your deal, still holdin’ a grudge over that time you got sloshed and paraded around in your undies?”

“Shut up! I’ll whip up a spell to blast those extra ‘memories’ right outta your head, so just you wait!”

Tampering with memories is taboo magic through and through, but if I could snag a chance to fool the eyes of Oda Laguna, that’d be enough. Even if it’s a one-shot opportunity, it’s worth developing for that alone.

“Hell, maybe at this rate, I should just wipe all the extra ‘memories’ of me from Reid’s head—it’d save me trouble down the line. Our first meeting and all... total embarrassment for me...”

“Hey-hey, Mistress, you done yet—?”

As I grumbled under my breath, Shaula came over, fidgeting impatiently.

Behind her, the sandcastles she and Reid had vied to build were basically just piled-up mounds of sand with some half-hearted hollowing out—crude as could be. At least, they looked miles away from the artistic masterpieces he’d described, but I had to give points for effort.

“That said, I’m no expert judge myself. This’ll just be a layman’s take, but...”

“That’s fine by me! What I want’s the victor’s medal... So I can strut over to that annoyin’ Reid with it, then full-dive into Master’s chest! ――Oh, whoops.”

Shaula squeezed herself tight in a surge of excitement, arching her back dramatically. ――Her head smacked right into the sandcastle, cracking the fragile balance it had been holding.

It might not have measured up to the real castle, but the sandy lump was big enough to pass for a house. And as it crumbled, it dragged Reid’s neighboring castle down with it in a chain reaction collapse.

“Hey, you jerk! My castle too!”

“W-Wah, accident! Total accident! Act of God!”

“Nah, even I gotta say that’s pushin’ it... Wait, huh? Echidna-chan? Echidna-chan? Where’d ya go?”

“Eh? G-Gyahhh! Mistress, I’m dead! Buried alive! Sealed away for three thousand years with Tutankhamun’s treasures!”

“Ka-kka-kka-kka! Nearly dyin’ from sand play? Still just a kid, huh, you!”

Shaula’s half-hearted wail of distress and Reid’s enraging idiot-laugh rang out over the mess I’d gotten caught in—too slow to escape the collapse, now fully swallowed by the castle’s ruins.

Listening to it all from under the sand,

“W-Why... does the greatest ‘witch’ on earth... have to go through this...”

I could only claw weakly at the sand, stewing in resentment as I waited to be dug out.

――A side note: When he got back and showed off his own sandcastle, it was something else—leagues beyond what Shaula or Reid could compete with, for the record.

～Fin～
